title: Should you host your AI-built app on Vercel? Understand costs at scale and vendor lock-in before accepting the AI's default recommendation

tools.name: Vercel

tools.name: Supabase
tools.detail: Also commonly AI-recommended; same caution applies

tools.name: Next.js
tools.detail: AI tends to build on it unless pushed elsewhere

claims: AI tools recommend Vercel and Supabase very often; that does not mean they are right for you
Vercel is built by the Next.js team; starts inexpensive/free, easy to configure and connect services
Risk: what happens when it is no longer free, when you hit N users or app size, when services must connect to other things
Vendor lock-in can cost money and services down the road
how_to_steps: Before accepting Vercel, learn what it does and does not do
Ask your AI: what happens when it's not free? What will it cost at X users / app size? How will connected services work later?
Have that conversation before choosing any hosting vendor

relevance.why: Generic but real concern for a solo founder shipping Next.js apps: Vercel/Supabase bills at scale and portability. Nothing new for someone who already picks infra deliberately.

implement_score.why: Cheap habit: add a 'cost at 1K/10K/100K users and exit plan' question to the Claude Code project kickoff / CLAUDE.md infra checklist. No tooling needed.
